The kind plan_credits exists in the router and the order (packages/billing/src/router.ts:87-91) but nothing saves one.

The first choice: human.notify_prefs.billing_order, a list of kinds set by Move up / Move down in Settings -> Advanced -> 'Claude: which to use first' (apps/ui/src/pages/BillingOrderSection.tsx:129-259, POST /settings/billing-order, packages/runtime/src/daemon/billing-order-routes.ts:140-171, settings.set billing_order low risk, packages/commands/src/commands/settings.ts:424-438). 'When my first choice runs out mid-session': human.notify_prefs.mid_session_limit, wait (default) or use_other (packages/runtime/src/session/billing.ts:91-101; spec packages/commands/src/commands/settings.ts:444-462, medium risk, use_other asks a yes); a generic row under Advanced (packages/runtime/src/daemon/settings-view.ts:150-158) whose choices read 'Wait for its reset; the tasks start by themselves' / 'Use the other one at once (may cost money)' (apps/ui/src/pages/SettingsFields.tsx:116-119). BillingRouter.pick (packages/billing/src/router.ts:166-340) skips other_human, disabled, purpose, tier, cloud_runner, unavailable (no credential), refused (:221-227), cooldown = resting after a usage limit (:228-239), plan_share = the subscription at or above its share cap (:240-252), monthly_limit = a source's own monthly cap (:253-260). Under waitOnRest only resting and refused first choices hold the pick ('unavailable' with details.waitFor, :284-321); plan_share and monthly_limit always move to the next source, the API key included (wave7g6-triage owner_questions[2]).

The plan-share cap: 0.95 written on the seeded subscription row (billing-pick.ts:49, :94), not settable; the share is the month's API-equivalent subscription spend over the allowance the person enters in Settings -> Advanced -> 'Claude subscription allowance' (apps/ui/src/pages/PlanAllowanceSection.tsx, POST /settings/plan-allowance; FORERUNNER_PLAN_USD_MONTHLY overrides). Mid-run the hooks enforce it as the caps' 'plan' level (packages/billing/src/caps.ts:193-198, :255-279): the run pauses (ADR 0112), the budget card 'paused at the share of your Claude subscription that Forerunner may use' (packages/runtime/src/session/budget-card.ts:99-101), the session ends (budget-pause.ts:187-189) and the task goes on by itself at the next month (budget-card.ts:416-417); the next pick meanwhile skips the subscription and serves on the key.

The key's own monthly cap (limits.monthlyUsdMicro, packages/billing/src/sources.ts:24) is read by the router (router.ts:253-260) and Settings (billing-order-routes.ts:98-99) but nothing writes it: no screen or command sets it. The person's monthly spending cap (Basics, CHF 150 by default, packages/billing/src/defaults.ts:11) is a budget stop for all spending, counting the subscription's API-equivalent estimates too (caps.ts:177-180 sums every ledger kind); it is no credential run-out.

A run a credential stops mid-way (provider_usage_limit or provider_auth): the executor rests or marks the source (executor.ts:1693-1712, billing-pick.ts:698-786), asks what comes next (nextCredential, executor.ts:2135-2148) and returns usage_limit; its work is kept as a work-in-progress commit on the task's branch (packages/capabilities/src/githost/pr-executor.ts:696-701). The runner gives the task back to ready without a try; with continuesOn (use_other, or a refused first choice under use_other) it puts the task back at the head of the queue in the same session, else the task waits and the session goes on with what can run (packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:1886-1927, at most 3 moves, :710).

The next run of such a task is briefed '## The previous attempt / It failed: <the limit in words>' (packages/runtime/src/session/task-context.ts:249-262): only paused and budget_exceeded runs read as kept work ('## Where the last run stopped ... continue from it'), so the run on the other credential is not told to continue from its kept commit.

Chat, planning, reviews and the background jobs (RoutedProvider, packages/runtime/src/provider/routed.ts): the pick passes no waitOnRest (:282-292), so a resting or refused first choice is skipped at once; a call that meets a usage limit or a refusal before it streamed is made once more on the next source (:236-262). Settings' row says 'Chat, planning and reviews always use the next one' (settings-view.ts:155-156). A chat turn no credential can serve replies 'I could not answer (<message>)' (packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1004-1007).

Credential waits: the source keeps limits.restingUntil, refusedAt/refusedKey/refusedWhy and waiting [{projectId, agentId, since}] (sources.ts:22-63), all persisted; before every scheduler tick the wake takes the projects whose source serves again (takeReady, billing-pick.ts:827-900) and starts a 'budget_reset' session with the project's full budget (compose.ts:3555-3630); saving a new credential ends a refusal at once (credentialSaved, billing-pick.ts:902-923, compose.ts:3634-3647). The Start check only reads; a Start keeps a wait (TR-2, compose.ts:3648-3666, start-blocked.ts:75-87). d1109-starts-engine (D6) turns the wake into a continuation of the session the person started.

What the person reads of a wait or a switch: the session log's billing.fallback line from stoppedRunSentence ('Your Claude subscription reached its usage limit; "X" waits until 15:40 (your subscription's limit) and starts by itself.' / '... continues on your API key now.', credential-wait.ts:289-304; event-lines.ts:500-501); the task row 'Waits until 15:40, your subscription's limit' and the project status 'Waiting until 15:40 (your subscription's limit): 2 tasks' (credential-wait.ts:208-226, project-status.ts:279-296); the Start dialog's blocked sentence (start-blocked.ts:75-87); Settings' per-credential status ('Can be used now', 'Resting until …; waiting work starts by itself then', 'Refused: …', BillingOrderSection.tsx:25-50). No notification is sent for a switch or a wait (packages/runtime/src/notifications/producers.ts has no credential producer); the session end notification says a wait as part of its result.

A refused credential: one Inbox card per credential, filed once ('Anthropic refused your API key' / '… your Claude sign-in'; body 'Save a new one in Settings. The work that needs it waits and starts by itself then.' or, when another credential takes the work, '... Until then your tasks go on with your API key, which costs money.'; link 'Save a new key' -> /setup) (credential-wait.ts:320-351, request-words.ts:1008-1040); blocking, so it is an urgent notification (producers.ts:183-193). The provider's reason is stored redacted (refusedWhy, billing-pick.ts:752) and never shown. A refused credential is never called again until a different one is in the vault (fingerprint, billing-pick.ts:201-221); the probe makes no network call (billing-pick.ts:157-198).

Spend per credential: every ledger row names its billing source and kind; subscription rows are API-equivalent estimates with the plan share (packages/billing/src/ledger.ts:258-274). Settings shows each credential's month (BillingOrderSection.tsx:53-60). The session page and result give one total; nothing says which credential paid or what a switch cost (d1109-sessions adds 'CHF … on your API key' per session).

Restart: the order, the mid-session setting, rests, refusals and waits are all in the state store and survive; the wake runs before every scheduler tick after a restart too (ADR 0100 points 4 and 9). Nothing records a person's answer about moving to the other credential, since nothing asks.
design:
The person sets one choice, and every model call follows it. A person with no technical knowledge reads it in one look: which Claude works first, and what happens when it runs out.

1. WHAT A PERSON CAN HAVE. At most one Claude subscription (through Claude Code, no money per use within the plan's limits) and one API key (money per use). The choice below is about these two; plan credits (never saved today) follow the API key wherever the key goes.

2. THE ONE CHOICE: Settings -> Basics -> 'Which Claude does the work' (directly under Accounts and keys; it replaces Advanced's 'Claude: which to use first' list and the 'When my first choice runs out mid-session' row). One intro line: 'Your Claude subscription has no cost per use within your plan's limits; your API key costs money per use.' Then five choices, each a label that shows the order and one line (all lines <= 100 characters):
  (a) 'Subscription, then wait' — 'When your subscription runs out, work waits until it resets. Nothing moves to your API key.' (the default, today's 'Wait')
  (b) 'Subscription, then ask me' — 'When your subscription runs out, one card asks: go on with your API key at its cost, or wait.'
  (c) 'Subscription, then API key' — 'When your subscription runs out, your API key takes over at once. You are told the cost.'
  (d) 'API key, then subscription' — 'Your API key does the work, at a cost per use. When it runs out, your subscription takes over.'
  (e) 'API key only' — 'Your API key does all the work, at a cost per use. When it runs out, work waits.' (for a person who keeps the plan for their own use)
Below the choices, the order as it stands now, one row per credential: its name, its role under the choice ('Does the work' / 'After you say yes, when your subscription runs out' / 'Takes over when your subscription runs out' / 'Only for a task your subscription cannot do' / 'Not used'), its state now ('Works now' / 'At its limit until 15:40' / 'Share used until 1 Dec' / 'Refused: save a new sign-in' [link] / 'Not saved') and its month ('34% of this month's allowance used' / 'CHF 2.10 this month'). Then one line, computed when shown, of what happens next: 'If your subscription runs out, you are asked before your API key is used.' or, while it is out, 'Your subscription is at its limit until 15:40. Answer the card to use your API key or wait. [Answer]'. One line says what running out means: 'Runs out means: its usage limit is reached, the share of your subscription Forerunner may use is used, or Anthropic refuses it (you are then told how to fix it).' For the subscription-first choices one footnote: 'A task only your API key can do here (one that must ask you) still runs on it; the plan card says so.' With one credential saved, the five choices fold away and one sentence says what happens ('Only your Claude subscription is saved: it does the work, and when it runs out work waits until it resets. Save an API key to choose what happens then. [Save an API key]'); the stored choice is kept for when the second is saved. Choosing (a) or (b) acts at once; (c), (d) and (e) put work on money without asking, so the change card asks a yes once ('Use "Subscription, then API key"? When your subscription runs out, work goes on with your API key at once, at a cost per use.'). Changes lists every change with Undo; chat can change it in words with the same read-back. Advanced keeps what is detail: 'What each can do here', the subscription allowance and 'Code tasks that need commands'.

3. MIGRATION, nothing a person chose changes. The choice is stored as human.notify_prefs.credential_policy. While it is unset it is derived, at every read, from today's two settings: no order or the subscription first + wait -> (a); the subscription first + use the other one -> (c); the API key (or plan credits) first + wait -> (e); the API key first + use the other one -> (d). The old keys are never rewritten (an older build reads its own); once credential_policy is stored it wins, and an Undo of an old billing_order or mid_session_limit row is refused with 'This was replaced by "Which Claude does the work"; change it there.' The one visible change for a person who never moved the order: chat, planning and reviews now follow the same choice (they were on the API key first, which cost money per reply); Settings says 'Chat, planning and reviews follow this choice too.' (owner question 2).

4. WHAT RUNNING OUT IS, and when it ends. Four ways, each said in the person's words: a usage limit ('at its limit until 15:40'; ends at the reset the provider named, else after an hour, ADR 0100 point 4), Forerunner's share of the subscription ('share used until 1 Dec'; ends at the month's start or when the person raises the allowance), a key's own monthly cap (no screen sets one today; ends at the month's start), a refusal ('Anthropic refused your Claude sign-in'; ends when a different credential is saved). The person's monthly spending cap, the project's budget and the session's budget are budgets, not run-outs: they stop work on every credential as today (ADR 0112), never passed.

5. WHAT THE ENGINE DOES, for every call (task runs, their reviews, the plan from a brief, chat, the background jobs). The choice gives the order and what follows. The chooser's rule stays: a task only one credential can do properly runs on it whatever the choice ('API key only' never uses the subscription at all). When the credential the task would use first has run out:
  - go on ((c), (d)): the next credential serves at once. The first move of each run-out is told (point 9). If the next has run out too, the work waits for whichever comes back first.
  - ask first ((b)): if the person said yes for this run-out, the next serves (told once in the log, no notification: their own click is not echoed). Otherwise the work waits exactly as under wait, and one card asks (point 7). A background job never asks: it waits and says so in its own report.
  - wait ((a), (e)): nothing calls the other credential for work whose first choice is out, not a task, a review, a plan or a chat reply; the work waits and every place says until when. Work whose first choice is the other credential by the chooser runs.
In code: the router's hold covers all four run-outs (resting, refused, plan_share, monthly_limit; waitFor.reason limit | refused | share | key_month with until = the reset, null, or the month's start), the hold is on for wait and for ask without a yes, and the routed provider passes it like the task pick (CALL_FALLBACK_ORDER retired: one order for every purpose).

6. A TASK STOPPED MID-RUN. The run stops cleanly where it is (the hooks still stop it at the limit or the share; nothing is passed), its work is kept (the work-in-progress commit on its branch, or the folder), no try is counted and nothing is reviewed. Under go on, or after a yes, the task goes back to the head of the session's queue and continues on the next credential from its kept work in the same session (owner 7a: the stopped task is finished on the API key); its brief says so in exact words: '## Where the last run stopped' / 'The last run of this task stopped when its Claude credential reached its limit (or: was refused), before its work was done. Its work so far is in the folder you work in (kept as a commit of its own): continue from it, do not start again.' followed by its report as data and the files it changed, never '## The previous attempt / It failed'. Under wait, or before a yes, it waits; the session goes on with what can run and, when nothing can, ends to wait and goes on at the end of the run-out with what is left of its budget and promise (d1109-starts-engine's continuation; no new session starts without the person, D6). Reaching Forerunner's share mid-run is the same stop with reason share: no budget card, no 'goes on by itself next month' unless the choice says wait.

7. ASK FIRST, the card word for word (one per run-out, for every project, chat and planning together; Needs you, the Home list, the project's status 'Waiting for you: use your API key?' [Answer], and inline in the chat when a chat reply waits on it):
  title 'Use your API key until 15:40?' ('… until Wed 12 Nov, 05:00?', '… until 1 Dec?')
  body 'Your Claude subscription is at its limit until 15:40. Going on with your API key costs about CHF 0.90 for "Style the page" and 2 more.' (the share: 'Forerunner has used the share of your subscription you allow this month. Going on …'; a plan: '… costs about CHF 0.05 to draft the plan for "Quote page".'; chat only: '… Chat replies on your API key cost a few centimes each.'). The figure is the remaining estimate of the waiting work, capped at what is left of its session's budget.
  Use API key — 'Work goes on now with your API key until 15:40, about CHF 0.90. Each use costs money.'
  Wait — 'Nothing moves. At 15:40 your session goes on with your Claude subscription.' (no session waiting: 'Nothing moves. After 15:40 it runs at your next Start.'; the share: 'Nothing moves until 1 Dec, or until you raise the allowance in Settings.')
  Use API key writes the yes on the first choice's billing row (limits.goOn: the run-out it answers, until the reset, or for a refusal until a new credential), so it survives a restart; then the session that ended to wait goes on now as the person's own start (D6), a plan that waited is drafted, and chat answers. Done line 'Done: your API key does the work until 15:40; your session goes on now.' Wait records the answer, so no second card comes for this run-out; nothing moves; Done line 'Done: nothing moves. Your session goes on at 15:40 with your subscription.' Unanswered, the card stays; nothing moves. When the run-out ends (the reset passes, the month turns, the allowance is raised, a new credential is saved) the yes ends with it, an open card closes ('Closed: your Claude subscription can work again.'), and the next run-out asks again. The Start dialog asks in place: with the first choice out and no answer, its Start becomes two buttons, 'Use API key' ('Runs now on your API key, about CHF 0.90; nothing passes this session's budget.') and 'Start at 15:40' ('Runs on your Claude subscription once it resets.'); the first records the same yes and closes the card.

8. A REFUSAL (owner 7c) follows the same choice as running out and always informs: one card per credential, one urgent notification (the card's), the link 'Save a new sign-in' / 'Save a new key' to the setup assistant ('The setup assistant checks it with Anthropic and saves it.'). Its body says why in plain words, from a category of Anthropic's answer, never its text ('The sign-in has expired or was signed out.', 'The key is not valid or was deleted.', 'The key may not use this model or workspace.', else 'Anthropic did not accept it.'), then what happens under the choice: wait '… Save a new one in Settings; until then the work waits.'; go on '… Save a new one in Settings; until then your API key does the work, at a cost per use.'; ask '… Save a new one in Settings, or go on with your API key until then (about CHF 0.90)?' with Use API key / Wait (after an answer the card stays as the fix-it card with the answer in words, since the fix is still needed). The second choice refused while the first works: '… Save a new one in Settings to use it again; your subscription goes on with the work.' A refused credential is never called again until a different one is in the vault (no retry that could lock an account); the probe stays offline.

9. A SWITCH IS TRANSPARENT (go on, or a yes): once per run-out the session log says 'Your Claude subscription is at its limit until 15:40; "Style the page" goes on with your API key now, from where it stopped.'; a move onto money (to the API key) sends one notification, normal urgency, not for a yes the person just gave: title 'Quote page: work goes on with your API key', body 'Your Claude subscription is at its limit until 15:40. Your API key costs money: about CHF 0.90 for what is left of this session.' (folded into the refused card's notification for a refusal; none for a move onto the subscription, which costs no money); the session page shows 'On your API key since 14:20 (your subscription's limit): CHF 0.42 so far.'; the result adds 'Your API key took over at 14:20 (your subscription's limit): CHF 0.42 of CHF 0.62.'; the task's run in its drawer reads 'on your API key'; the run indicator reads 'Quote page · the coder works on "Style the page" on your API key · 4 min'. Every call is booked to the credential that paid (ledger rows by source, as today). When the first choice is back, a running session says 'Your Claude subscription can work again; the next tasks use it.' and the next task uses it; a run is never moved mid-way (ADR 0100 point 3).

10. WHERE THE PERSON SEES IT, without new clutter: Settings (the choice, the order, each credential's state, the next line); the Start dialog (one line under the plan sentence: 'On your Claude subscription. If it runs out, you are asked before your API key is used.'; with the first out: 'Your subscription is at its limit until 15:40, so this runs on your API key (about CHF 0.90).' under go on, the two buttons under ask, the wait sentence under wait); the plan card (one line at its foot: 'Runs on your Claude subscription; if it runs out, you are asked before your API key is used.'); the project status and task rows (every wait in words: 'Waiting until 1 Dec (your subscription's share): 2 tasks [Change the allowance]', 'Waits for your answer: use your API key? [Answer]'); Needs you (the card); the session page and the run indicator (the switch); chat under wait: 'Claude cannot answer until 15:40: your subscription is at its limit, and you chose to wait. I can still add, move and start tasks.'; chat under go on: a note under the reply 'Answered with your API key: your subscription is at its limit until 15:40.'. No reminder and no app-wide bar for a wait (the owner: 'We don't need notifications like that').

11. RESTART: the choice, the derived choice, a yes (limits.goOn), an answered Wait, the open card, rests, refusals and waits are in the state store; a yes still holds after a restart until the run-out ends, and a card whose run-out ended while the app was closed closes at the first wake; a switch is told once per run-out (dedupe key per source and run-out), not again after a restart.

12. MONEY AND SECURITY: no budget, wrap-up line, monthly cap or share is passed (the hooks are unchanged; a task continued on the key is held by the same session, task, project and month caps; the card's figure is capped at what is left of the session's budget); under wait, before a yes and after Wait, the tests assert zero calls on the other credential; a key never runs through Claude Code (the continued run uses the loop driver in the sandbox, ADR 0100 point 5); card, chat and page text never become instructions (the card's words are built from facts, chat answers it with its option strings through the command registry); Anthropic's refusal text is never shown or logged unredacted (only its category is shown).

13. CLOSES wave7g6-triage owner_questions[1..3]: (1) under wait only the tasks whose first choice is out wait; the others run (as built); (2) a share or a key's monthly cap counts as running out and holds under wait and ask (b); (3) a refused credential follows the choice as if it ran out, and its card says what, why and how. ADR 0100 point 15's 'session lead's default' becomes the owner's rule.
alternatives_rejected: Two questions (which first; what then) as two radio groups: needs the person to combine them in their head and allows 'API key, then ask me', which protects no money (the subscription costs nothing per use); five full sentences, each naming its order, read in one look.

A per-project choice (built meanwhile: one for all projects): the credentials and the plan's limits are the person's, shared by every project; per project, 'which works now' would depend on the page you are on. Owner question.
One ask card per stopped task or per session: the owner asked for 'one card'; a run-out stops many tasks at once; one answer covers every project, chat and planning until the first choice is back.
Asking before every chat reply: chat is where the person is waiting; the same one card covers chat, shown inline.
Keeping 'chat, planning and reviews always use the next one' (ADR 0100 point 4): moves work onto money while the app says it waits (owner 7b).

Keeping the share pause as a budget card: two behaviours for one run-out (the card says it waits, the next pick moves to the key); the hooks still stop the run at the share, only what follows changes.

Exposing the key's own monthly cap in the section: a second money number beside the monthly spending cap that already bounds all spending; owner question, the dormant field counts as a run-out meanwhile.
Moving a running run back to the subscription when it resets: a run is never re-routed (ADR 0100 point 3) and the drivers differ; the next task uses it.
An app-wide bar 'Claude is at its limit': a reminder-like element the owner does not want; the status lines, the run indicator, the Start dialog and Settings say it where the person acts.
A notification for every switch or every task that moves: once per run-out, and only for a move onto money.
Keeping the yes in memory: Quit stops the service daily (ADR 0094); a yes forgotten at the next start would ask again or move without one.
Trying a refused credential again after a while to see whether it works: repeated refused sign-ins can lock the person's account; only a different saved credential ends a refusal.
A one-off 'Use API key' button in the Start dialog under 'wait': the person chose wait; the dialog's line links to the choice instead.
Rewriting billing_order and mid_session_limit into the new key at upgrade: an older build after a downgrade would read nothing; deriving at read keeps every stored choice and needs no migration step.

decisions: C-1: One setting, human.notify_prefs.credential_policy, five values: subscription_then_wait (default), subscription_then_ask, subscription_then_key, key_then_subscription, key_only; one pure function credentialPolicyOf(prefs) that reads it, else derives it from billing_order and mid_session_limit (no order or subscription first + wait -> subscription_then_wait; subscription first + use_other -> subscription_then_key; api_key or plan_credits first + wait -> key_only; + use_other -> key_then_subscription), and ruleOf(policy) = {order, then: wait | ask | go_on, kinds allowed}. settings.set credential_policy: medium risk, narrows to the first two (act at once), the other three ask a yes; display = the label, effect = the line. Why: the owner's 'framework ... and then the system just does it'; deriving at read keeps every stored choice ('without changing what a person already chose') and needs no migration step.

C-2: The router's hold covers every run-out: resting (limit), refused, plan_share (share) and monthly_limit (key_month), each with its until (the reset, null, the next month's start in UTC); it holds for then = wait and for then = ask without a yes, and a yes for the held source's current run-out lets the pick go on; 'kinds allowed' takes the subscription out for key_only. Why: owner question 2 answered (b); 7b.

C-3: Every call reads the policy at its pick: the executor's billingRequestOf replaces midSessionLimitOf, and the routed provider (chat, interactive, critic, batch) passes the same hold; CALL_FALLBACK_ORDER is retired, so there is one order. A background job (batch) never asks: ask counts as wait for it, with no card. Why: 7b; no hidden second order (D5-3).

C-4: Under wait, and under ask before a yes or after Wait, nothing calls the other credential for work whose first choice is out; tasks the chooser puts on the other credential run (as built). Why: 7b; owner question 1 answered (a).

C-5: Ask first: one card per run-out (key credential:go_on; one open per source and run-out; words computed when shown; options 'Use API key' / 'Wait'). Use API key writes limits.goOn {reason, until, refusedKey?, at} on the first choice's row with the version check (updateSourceLimits), then starts the waiting continuation(s) as the person's start (d1109-starts-engine's port) and drafts a plan that waited; Wait records the answer on the card so no second card comes. Both survive a restart. The card closes by itself when the run-out ends. Why: the owner's 'after asking human'; one card; a yes lasts the run-out so the person is not asked per task.

C-6: A task stopped mid-run (limit, refusal, share) keeps its work and, under go on or a yes, goes back to the head of the queue and continues on the next credential in the same session; the brief's previous-run section reads it as kept work with the exact text in the acceptance, never 'It failed'. Why: 7a ('the task to be completed by the API'); a run that redoes kept work spends twice.

C-7: Reaching Forerunner's share mid-run (the hooks' 'plan' stop, unchanged) is returned as a credential stop with reason share, its handoff kept on the run: no budget card, the session does not end for it, and the policy decides what follows. Open budget cards at 'plan' from before the upgrade keep their wake. Why: one behaviour per run-out; no limit passed.

C-8: A switch is told once per run-out: the log line, a session fact (first switch time, from and to, reason, until) for the session page and the result, and one notification (credential_switched, normal urgency) only for a move onto money and only when the person did not just say yes (design §5.11). Why: 7a 'transparent'; the owner wants no notifications about waiting, and a move onto the subscription costs nothing.

C-9: The refused card follows the policy and informs: why in plain words from a category of the provider's answer (refusalWhy: expired sign-in, invalid or deleted key, not allowed for this model or workspace, else 'Anthropic did not accept it.'), the fix (the setup link), and what the work does now under the choice; under ask it carries the Use API key / Wait question and stays open as the fix-it card after the answer. Never the provider's text. Why: 7c; secrets never shown.
C-10: Chat says a credential wait in words (wait, ask, refused, both out) and, under go on, a note under the reply; the ask is the same card shown inline. Why: design §5.8; the person is in the chat.

C-11: The end of a run-out ends the yes and closes an open card ('Closed: your Claude subscription can work again.'), and a running session says once 'Your Claude subscription can work again; the next tasks use it.'; a run already on the other credential finishes there. Why: order means order; ADR 0100 point 3.

adr: <next free> (0119 if the run C designs take 0114 to 0118; the session lead renumbers) — Which Claude does the work: one credential policy. The person picks one of five choices whose labels show the order (Subscription, then wait [default]; Subscription, then ask me; Subscription, then API key; API key, then subscription; API key only), stored as human.notify_prefs.credential_policy and, while unset, derived at every read from billing_order and mid_session_limit, so no stored choice changes. Every model call follows it: task runs, reviews, the plan from a brief, chat and the background jobs (CALL_FALLBACK_ORDER retired: one order). Running out is a usage limit, Forerunner's share of the subscription, a key's own monthly cap or a refusal; for each the choice decides: go on with the next credential at once (told once per run-out: the log, the session page, the result, one notification for a move onto money), ask first (one card per run-out with the cost and the time it ends: Use API key / Wait; the yes is kept on the first choice's row until the run-out ends; a background job only waits), or wait (nothing calls the other credential). A refusal follows the same rule and its card says what was refused, why (a category, never the provider's text) and how to fix it. A task stopped mid-run keeps its work and, when the choice lets it, continues from it on the next credential in the same session, briefed to continue; a share reached mid-run is a credential stop, not a budget card. A wait inside the session the person started ends it and it goes on at the end of the run-out (d1109-starts-engine's ADR); 'Use API key' is a person's start of that continuation. Kept: the chooser (a task only one credential can do runs there), a key never in Claude Code (ADR 0100 point 5), every budget and cap. Closes wave7g6-triage owner_questions[1..3]. Amends ADR 0044 (the share is a run-out), 0098 (non-task calls follow the choice), 0100 (points 2, 4, 10, 15 and the amendments of 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-08) and 0112 (the subscription's share).
